title: K-flat complex of modules on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. A cochain complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] is *acyclic* if all its cohomology sheaves $H^i(\mathcal F^\bullet)$, computed in the abelian category of $\mathcal O$-modules, vanish [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. A cochain complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules is *K-flat* if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is acyclic. A *K-flat resolution* of a complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $\mathcal K^\bullet$ K-flat.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 06YN (sites-cohomology.tex, Section 06YL), which defines K-flatness exactly as stated; 'K-flat resolution' is not part of 06YN but is the term used in 06YS, and is kept. Split by one level: the notions are cochain complexes of O-modules (new def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, Mathlib leaf CochainComplex (SheafOfModules R) ℤ, Stacks 010V/0114), cohomology sheaves and acyclicity (new def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules, Mathlib leaf HomologicalComplex.Acyclic / homology, Stacks 0115(2)), the total tensor complex (existing def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, Mathlib leaf), and quasi-isomorphisms (new def-pc-quasi-iso-modules, Mathlib leaf QuasiIso, Stacks 0115(1)). The statement's citations of def-weil-abstract-derived-category (used only for cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms, not for the derived category) were replaced by these finer nodes; the wording is otherwise unchanged. The definition does not use flatness of modules; the flat-module notion needed by lem-pc-kflat-resolution was created as def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules (Stacks 03ER(3), unsplit: Mathlib has only Module.Flat over a ring) but is not a dependency of this node. Mathlib has no K-flat notion (only CochainComplex.IsKInjective / IsKProjective).
